content:
I have a question about the new String API, which came up in #37391 (moving the create_module_deprecation script to the new API).
Given s : String, the script used to do s.trim.splitOn "\n" (to obtain a list of Strings --- string slices would be equally fine). Now, this warns about Strimg.trim being deprecated --- but String.trimAscii returns a String.Slice, and there is no way to split a String.Slice. What's the intended replacement?
There's docs#String.Slice.split and docs#String.Slice.lines (and corresponding functions for docs#String) though? In fact, docs#String.splitOn is a legacy function subsumed by docs#String.split.
I'll also note that there are a few places where you wrote log.dropWhile (·.isWhitespace) and should've written log.dropWhile (!·.isWhitespace).

Thanks a lot, that's very helpful. Do you also know the idiomatic way to get the last element of an iterator (given sufficient conditions)? Is the point that iterators can be infinite in general, which means a last element is not defined in general? (For know, I'm converting to a list and then taking the last element. I'm all ears if there is a better way.)
Or iter.fold (fun _ x => x) default if you know it exists
Do you find that more readable? (To me, it's less obvious what it does, and longer also.)
This is an honest question: perhaps this depends on your amount of Lean metaprogramming/functional programming/etc done so far.
Yeah, I'd also prefer toList.getLast? unless you put it in a definition Std.Iter.last?.
